questions.q: Why does Driftwood open a new AWS account at all?
options: To migrate the storefront app fully to AWS
Scoped strictly to backup/DR — holding a copy of the app's data, per Casey's original scope
To run a second production environment load-balanced with Azure
Because Azure was being decommissioned
questions.explain: Casey's Lesson 1 scope is explicit: AWS exists only to hold a copy of the app's data, not to run the application.

questions.q: What does the `aws_s3_bucket_versioning` resource protect against?
options: Public internet access to the bucket
A bad overwrite or delete silently destroying a prior backup version
High storage costs
Slow retrieval speed from Glacier
questions.explain: Versioning means a corrupted or bad backup upload doesn't destroy the previous good version.

questions.q: What is the difference between the IAM policy on the replication role and a bucket policy?
options: There is no difference; they do the same thing
The IAM policy says what the replication role is allowed to do; a bucket policy would say who, beyond that role, can reach the bucket at all
A bucket policy only applies to EC2 instances
IAM policies are optional and bucket policies are required
questions.explain: IAM policies are identity-based (what a principal can do); bucket policies are resource-based (who can reach the resource).

questions.q: What two hardening steps does Theo intend to add before go-live, but doesn't get to in this lesson?
options: Enabling versioning and adding a lifecycle rule
A bucket policy restricting access to just the replication role, and explicitly enabling S3 Block Public Access on the bucket
Deleting the bucket and recreating it in a different region
Switching the storage class to Glacier immediately
questions.explain: The intended restricting bucket policy and an explicit S3 Block Public Access setting both get deferred and never picked back up.

questions.q: At the end of this lesson, is the S3 bucket actually being exploited or publicly breached?
options: Yes, data has already leaked
No — nothing looks obviously wrong in the console; it's simply left on a broader-than-intended default access configuration
Yes, but only Priya knows about it
The bucket doesn't exist yet
questions.explain: This lesson plants a realistic gap — a deferred hardening step — not an active exploit. It will surface later during a routine review.
